Actually, that's not correct. `typeof null` still returns `'object'` in all modern JavaScript engines, including the latest versions of Node.js. This behavior was not changed in ES6 or any subsequent ECMAScript version.

You can verify this in any current Node.js version:
```javascript
console.log(typeof null); // outputs: 'object'
```

This quirk is explicitly documented in the ECMAScript specification and remains for backward compatibility. It's one of the most famous "gotchas" in JavaScript and is intentionally preserved.

So my original answer stands: if you want to check for actual objects (excluding null), you need to guard against null explicitly: `v !== null && typeof v === 'object'`.
